item.title: Sunny skies and crisp nights ahead for Escambia County through weekend
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: North Escambia is in for a stretch of classic fall weather over the next several days, with plenty of sunshine and comfortable conditions expected through the weekend, according to local forecasts. Daytime highs will reach the upper 70s through the end of the work week before cooling slightly to the lower 70s by Saturday. Nights will be crisp,…
item.content:encoded:
North Escambia is in for a stretch of classic fall weather over the next several days, with plenty of sunshine and comfortable conditions expected through the weekend, according to local forecasts.

Daytime highs will reach the upper 70s through the end of the work week before cooling slightly to the lower 70s by Saturday. Nights will be crisp, dipping into the upper 40s, with a reinforcing northeast breeze helping to keep temperatures down.

The forecast calls for unbroken sunshine throughout the period, making it an ideal window for outdoor activities before cooler air moves in.

item.title: Storm Recovery Help Available Through Friday in Escambia County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Residents in North Escambia still dealing with storm damage can access free cleanup and repair assistance through at least the end of this week. Crisis Cleanup is operating a hotline at 800-451-1954 through Friday, October 30, offering free volunteer help with tree removal, tarps, and debris clearing. The service connects homeowners with trained…
item.content:encoded:
Residents in North Escambia still dealing with storm damage can access free cleanup and repair assistance through at least the end of this week.

Crisis Cleanup is operating a hotline at 800-451-1954 through Friday, October 30, offering free volunteer help with tree removal, tarps, and debris clearing. The service connects homeowners with trained volunteers who can tackle the labor-intensive work that often follows severe weather.

God's Pit Crew is also responding to storm damage in the area. The organization handles tree removal, debris cleanup, and roof tarping through either phone contact at 434-836-4472 or an online intake form at form.jotform.com/262828197747070.

Local officials remind residents that these volunteer networks work fastest when homeowners contact them promptly—both organizations' resources are in high demand following storms. Those needing assistance should reach out as soon as possible to secure a spot before the October 30 deadline.

item.content:encoded:
Faculty at Kingsfield Elementary School in North Escambia are banding together to support two colleagues battling breast cancer. Teacher Rachel Owens was recently diagnosed with the disease, joining music teacher Agie Sulls, who is already undergoing treatment for the same illness.

The show of solidarity from the school community reflects the close-knit bonds that often develop among educators working in the same building. Colleagues facing a health crisis of this magnitude frequently draw strength from workplace support systems that help ease the burden during extended treatment and recovery.

Breast cancer remains one of the most commonly diagnosed cancers among women in the United States, and diagnoses within tight-knit professional communities often prompt broader awareness and support efforts among staff members.

item.content:encoded:
A Flomaton man is facing multiple felony charges after authorities say he used counterfeit currency to purchase high-end electronics at Walmart stores across Escambia County.

According to North Escambia, the suspect allegedly passed dozens of fake bills while shopping at local retail locations. The investigation focused on transactions involving electronics purchases made with the counterfeit currency.

Details on the specific charges, arrest date, and the suspect's identity were not immediately available. The case remains under investigation by local law enforcement.

item.title: Conexon Connect Restores Fiber Network After Storm Damage in North Escambia
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Restoration efforts are accelerating across northern Escambia and Santa Rosa counties following recent storm damage to Conexon Connect's broadband infrastructure. The provider reports that all central fiber huts—the network's backbone distribution points—are now back online, according to North Escambia reporting. With all critical hub locations…
item.content:encoded:
Restoration efforts are accelerating across northern Escambia and Santa Rosa counties following recent storm damage to Conexon Connect's broadband infrastructure. The provider reports that all central fiber huts—the network's backbone distribution points—are now back online, according to North Escambia reporting.

With all critical hub locations restored, more than 50 specialized crews are now focused on reconnecting individual customer locations to the high-speed internet service. The effort underscores the scale of damage inflicted by the recent storm across the two-county region.

Connectionx Connect serves a substantial portion of the North Florida market, particularly in rural and underserved areas where fiber broadband is a critical utility for residents and businesses. The company has not yet announced a full restoration timeline, but the return of central hubs is considered a major milestone in getting service back to normal.

item.title: DeSantis Pushes Amendment 3 Property Tax Relief at Miami Roundtable
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis held a roundtable in Miami on Wednesday to build support for Amendment 3, a proposed constitutional amendment that would expand homestead exemptions and create a path toward eliminating non-school property taxes on homesteaded properties. According to the Governor's Press Office, DeSantis highlighted that property tax…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis held a roundtable in Miami on Wednesday to build support for Amendment 3, a proposed constitutional amendment that would expand homestead exemptions and create a path toward eliminating non-school property taxes on homesteaded properties.

According to the Governor's Press Office, DeSantis highlighted that property tax revenues across Florida's 67 counties have nearly doubled over the past seven years—from about $32 billion in 2019 to over $60 billion today—outpacing inflation and population growth. "Local governments are taking in almost twice as much money," DeSantis said, arguing that as the state has reduced its budget four years running, local governments should do the same.

Under Amendment 3, homeowners would see immediate relief through an expanded exemption on non-school property taxes, starting with up to $150,000 of a home's value in 2027 and rising to $250,000 in 2028, with future inflation adjustments. The Governor's office estimates an average Miami-Dade homeowner with a $250,000-plus home value could save roughly $2,500 annually once fully implemented. The amendment would also cap annual assessment increases on non-residential properties at 5%, down from 10%.

Miami-Dade County Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz joined DeSantis at the event, stating that tax relief and public safety are complementary, not competing priorities. She cited her office's $12 million in annual technology cost reductions as an example of government efficiency.

Details about the specific features, deployment timeline, and how the system will be integrated into dispatch protocols were not immediately available. The move reflects a growing trend among law enforcement agencies across Alabama and the Southeast to adopt drone technology for faster situational awareness and improved officer safety during initial response calls.

Foley, located in Baldwin County, is among a number of municipalities exploring how aerial platforms can complement traditional policing methods.

item.title: Cat Country 98.7 Wins Prestigious National Marconi Award
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Cat Country 98.7, Pensacola's locally owned and operated radio station, has won the prestigious Radio Station of the Year Marconi Award, presented by the National Association of Broadcasters. The station was chosen among medium-sized market radio stations nationwide for the honor. Station Owner and General Manager Mary Hoxeng accepted the award…
item.content:encoded:
Cat Country 98.7, Pensacola's locally owned and operated radio station, has won the prestigious Radio Station of the Year Marconi Award, presented by the National Association of Broadcasters. The station was chosen among medium-sized market radio stations nationwide for the honor.

Station Owner and General Manager Mary Hoxeng accepted the award last night at the Marconi Radio Awards Ceremony at Edison Ballroom in New York City during the National Association of Broadcasters Show. The NAB Marconi Awards, established in 1989 and named after inventor and Nobel Prize winner Guglielmo Marconi, are given annually to radio stations that recognize excellence in broadcasting.

According to Hoxeng, the award specifically recognized the station's efforts during the historic snowstorm experienced in January 2025. "This award was specifically awarded due to our team's efforts during the historic snowstorm we experienced from January of 2025," Hoxeng said.

The station's commitment to community service during the weather emergency was exemplary. "With the important leadership of Morning Host Brent Lane, everyone pitched in and kept our communities informed 24/7," Hoxeng explained.

Hoxeng expressed her pride in the Cat Country 98.7 team's dedication and teamwork. "I could not be prouder of our Cat Country 98.7 team!" she said.

During the January snowstorm, the station maintained round-the-clock coverage to ensure residents had access to critical information about weather conditions, road closures, emergency services, and community resources. This commitment to serving the Pensacola community during a time of crisis exemplified the station's mission and values.

The Marconi Awards remain one of the most prestigious honors in the broadcasting industry, recognizing stations that demonstrate outstanding achievement and community impact. Cat Country 98.7's recognition adds to the station's reputation as a vital news and information source for the Pensacola area.

The award underscores the importance of local radio stations in times of emergency and their role in keeping communities connected and informed.

item.title: Dog trained to sniff out sewage pollution in Mobile Bay waters
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Researchers at the Mobile Bay National Estuary Program are testing an unconventional but potentially powerful tool to protect regional waterways: a dog trained to detect human sewage contamination. The canine detection program leverages what scientists have long known—that dogs can sense things far beyond human ability. In this case, the specially…
item.content:encoded:
Researchers at the Mobile Bay National Estuary Program are testing an unconventional but potentially powerful tool to protect regional waterways: a dog trained to detect human sewage contamination.

The canine detection program leverages what scientists have long known—that dogs can sense things far beyond human ability. In this case, the specially trained dog is being deployed to help environmental teams identify pollution hotspots in local waters, according to WKRG News 5.

The initiative represents a novel approach to water quality monitoring in the Mobile Bay area, giving investigators a faster and potentially more cost-effective way to pinpoint sewage pollution before it spreads or causes environmental damage. The program is still in the exploration phase, but early results suggest canine detection could become a standard part of estuary protection efforts.

Motorgoers can check real-time traffic conditions at FL511.com or the Florida Highway Safety and Motor Vehicles traffic incidents portal at trafficincidents.flhsmv.gov.

item.title: ECUA starts air-release valve project Monday on 10th Avenue
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority will begin an air-release valve abandonment project Monday, Oct. 26, within Pensacola city limits, with work expected to wrap up within about a week, weather permitting. Air-release valves are critical components in water and wastewater pipeline systems that let trapped air escape and keep the system operating…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority will begin an air-release valve abandonment project Monday, Oct. 26, within Pensacola city limits, with work expected to wrap up within about a week, weather permitting.

Air-release valves are critical components in water and wastewater pipeline systems that let trapped air escape and keep the system operating properly. The abandonment process involves permanently shutting down a valve and sealing it as part of routine utility maintenance.

ECUA is partnering with Talcon Group, LLC, for the work, which will start on 10th Avenue and move eastward through the city. Residents in the affected areas should expect construction activity during the project period.

item.content:encoded:
The City of Pensacola is hosting a news conference Friday morning to unveil updates on shipbuilding initiatives at the Port of Pensacola, according to a media advisory from the city's public information office.

Mayor D.C. Reeves and federal partners will address attendees at 10 a.m. at the Port of Pensacola, 700 S. Barracks St. The event comes as local officials continue to pursue maritime manufacturing expansion in the region.

Members of the media planning to attend must RSVP to pio@cityofpensacola.com by 1 p.m. Thursday, Oct. 22. Port security will require a valid form of ID and confirmation on the RSVP list. Attendees should arrive at 9:30 a.m. and wear walking shoes, the advisory noted. Mayor Reeves will be available for interviews following the formal presentation.

item.title: Fried to challenge Trump visit with cost-of-living critique
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will host a press call Thursday morning to frame Donald Trump's planned Florida visit as a liability for Republican candidates, according to a media advisory released by the state party Wednesday. Fried plans to use the call—scheduled for 11 a.m. Thursday, ahead of Trump's Friday appearance—to highlight…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will host a press call Thursday morning to frame Donald Trump's planned Florida visit as a liability for Republican candidates, according to a media advisory released by the state party Wednesday.

Fried plans to use the call—scheduled for 11 a.m. Thursday, ahead of Trump's Friday appearance—to highlight economic pressures on Florida families and Trump's approval ratings among voters. The advisory notes that a majority of Floridians disapprove of Trump, positioning his visit as potentially damaging rather than helpful to GOP candidates heading into November.

The Democratic Party chair is specifically targeting U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, whose district Trump will visit. According to the advisory, Donalds has attempted to distance himself from Trump, including removing references to the president from his campaign website. Fried's office points to gas prices exceeding $4 per gallon, rising healthcare premiums, and grocery costs as evidence that Trump's economic record contradicts Donalds' public "A" rating of the Trump economy.

Journalists interested in joining the call can contact Evan Ecklund at evan@floridadems.org or (832) 977-8151.

item.title: Santa Rosa County Day of Caring invites community to support military, veterans

The county is inviting community members to decorate stockings and write holiday cards for area service members and veterans. Drop-in participation is welcome at any Santa Rosa…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County is asking residents to join a community-wide effort to brighten the holidays for local military personnel and veterans through the 2026 Day of Caring.

The county is inviting community members to decorate stockings and write holiday cards for area service members and veterans. Drop-in participation is welcome at any Santa Rosa County Public Library location during regular business hours on Friday, November 13. Supplies for the activity will be available while they last, according to a release from Santa Rosa County Communications and Media Relations.

The Day of Caring is a way for the community to show appreciation for those who have served. Library locations and hours can be found at santarosa.fl.gov/546/Locations-Hours. More details about the initiative are available at uwwf.org/day-caring-2026.

item.content:encoded:
Two men from the Mobile area have been arrested in connection with a shooting at a Spanish Fort bowling alley that injured one person earlier this month, according to WKRG News 5.

The incident occurred late at night at the bowling facility in Spanish Fort, Alabama. Investigators have linked the two suspects to the shooting, which resulted in at least one injury.

Details about the victims, the circumstances of the shooting, and the identities of the arrested men were not immediately available. The investigation remains ongoing.
